message.content: Today started slow and then turned out lovely. The morning was the usual coffee-and-laptop routine, but by late afternoon I wandered out into one of the older quarters of Copenhagen with a friend. The cobblestones felt good under my shoes and the light was that soft, slightly overcast kind that makes brick look warm. We passed a little cafe with red awnings — almost stopped, didn't, kept walking. After dinner I went down to the beach. The tide was out, the sky was pastel, and the sun sat right on the horizon line. I walked along the wet sand for a while; just my footprints. It felt good not to talk to anyone for a bit. By the time I turned around, the sun had dropped and the air had cooled enough to make me wish I'd brought a jacket. Worth it though. The kind of quiet evening I want to remember.
